deities: Lord Shiva as Baba Garibnath / Garibeshwara (Swayambhu Shivalinga - self-manifested)
festivals: Shravani Mela / Shravan month (Wikipedia lists 'Sharabani Mela' - likely Shravani)

history.dynasty: 18th century - built under patronage of Rani Bhubaneshwari Devi, queen of Darbhanga (per templeyatri.in)
history.summary: Garibnath Temple is one of Muzaffarpur's oldest Shiva temples, known as the 'Deoghar of Bihar' / second Baidyanath; the presiding deity Garibnath ('lord of the poor') is believed to relieve the problems of the poor. Legend: the site was a dense forest with seven banyan/peepal trees; when the landowner cut them, blood-red sap flowed from the sixth tree and the axe struck a hidden Shivalinga. Shiva appeared in the owner's dream that night, identifying himself as Baba Garibnath and ordering a temple built on the spot, with his devotee Shivdhari Pathak of Chapra appointed as priest. The Swayambhu lingam sits 1.5 ft below the sanctum floor with a silver-covered base and octagonal ashtadhatu argha; the main dome carries seven ashtadhatu kalashas; the complex has a sacred well (Chandrakupa) and shrines to Kartik, Ganesha, Radha-Krishna and Surya Narayana. The temple is under the Bihar State Board of Religious Trusts (per Wikipedia). Coordinates geocoded to Garib Asthan Road, corroborated by Wikipedia's 26.12444, 85.39028. name: Garib Sthan Mandir (Baba Garibnath Temple)
town_description: Muzaffarpur is a major city in north-central Bihar on the Burhi Gandak River, famous for its litchis and known as the 'Lychee Kingdom' of India.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (~75 km) is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Muzaffarpur Junction is the nearest railway station, close to the temple within the city.
travel.road: Located in the city centre on Garib Asthan Road, near Purani/Purna Bazaar; well connected by road.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Shravan month and Maha Shivaratri draw very large crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00 AM - 12:00 AM daily (per the temple's place listing - verify)
